'python3 scripts/lint-envvars.py $(git ls-files docker/scripts/**/*.sh)'
now exits 0 across the whole tree.

* fix(scripts): make 'Optional environment variables' end the required block for lint-dockerfile-envvars.py

lint-dockerfile-envvars.py's parse_script_requirements() only stopped
collecting header vars at the first non-comment line, so an
'# Optional environment variables:' sub-heading (itself a comment)
didn't terminate the block — everything listed under Optional was
swept into the required set and then checked against the invoking
Dockerfile's ARG/ENV declarations, which is the wrong direction for
vars that are explicitly optional.

This surfaced concretely on docker/Dockerfile.rocm: build-uccl.sh's
pre-existing 'Optional' UCCL_DEVICE was already being misclassified
as required on main, and this PR's newly-documented TARGETOS /
VIRTUAL_ENV (also Optional, added because lint-envvars.py needed them
declared) made it worse by adding two more spurious 'required' vars
that aren't ARG/ENV in that Dockerfile stage by design (TARGETOS is
set inline on the RUN line; VIRTUAL_ENV is documented as set by the
Python environment, not by callers).

Now '# Optional environment variables:' ends the required-var
collection, matching how ENVVARS.md rule 4 is updated to describe it.
lint-envvars.py is unaffected (it never distinguished the two
headings, and still shouldn't).

Verified:
- python3 scripts/lint-dockerfile-envvars.py docker/scripts docker/Dockerfile.rocm
  now reports only UCCL_PREFIX (down from UCCL_DEVICE + UCCL_PREFIX before
  this commit, TARGETOS + UCCL_DEVICE + VIRTUAL_ENV before this PR's own
  docs commit). UCCL_PREFIX is a separate, pre-existing failure independent
  of this PR and of the Required/Optional distinction: it's set via ENV in
  Dockerfile.rocm's parent 'base' stage and inherited by Docker's FROM base
  AS build semantics, but the linter tracks ARG/ENV per-stage with no
  inheritance modeling. Confirmed present on main before any of this PR's
  changes — left out of scope here, same as noted in the original PR
  description, since it needs a build-stage-inheritance-aware rewrite of
  DockerfileParser and I can't build/test the ROCm image locally.
- python3 scripts/lint-dockerfile-envvars.py docker/scripts docker/Dockerfile.cuda
  still passes (install-vllm.sh's Required-section CUDA_MINOR/FLASHINFER_VERSION
  aren't checked at all today because find_script_runs doesn't join RUN ... \
  continuations, so it never sees that invocation — a separate pre-existing
  gap, also unrelated to this fix, not touched here).
- python3 scripts/lint-envvars.py $(git ls-files 'docker/scripts/**/*.sh')
  still exits 0 across all 13 in-scope scripts.
- All other Dockerfiles (cpu, cuda, rdma-tools, xpu) validate cleanly.

* fix(scripts): model ENV inheritance across Dockerfile build stages

Per @diegocastanibm's request to pass the linters over every file:
docker/Dockerfile.rocm was the one remaining failure after the
Optional-heading fix, and it's a real gap in DockerfileParser rather
than a script/Dockerfile problem. build-uccl.sh needs UCCL_PREFIX,
which Dockerfile.rocm sets via 'ENV UCCL_PREFIX=...' in the base
stage — available in the build stage at actual build time via
Docker's normal 'FROM base AS build' semantics, but DockerfileParser
tracked ARG/ENV strictly per-stage with no inheritance, so it never
saw it.

Fixed by capturing the base image reference on each FROM line and,
when that reference matches an already-parsed stage name, seeding
the new stage's ENV set with a copy of that stage's ENV (ARG is
intentionally NOT inherited: per Docker's docs an ARG goes out of
scope at the end of the stage that declares it and does not cross a
FROM boundary, even into a stage built FROM that one). A templated
ref like 'FROM base-${TARGETARCH} AS vllm-build' (docker/Dockerfile.cpu)
won't literal-match a known stage name, so no inheritance is assumed
there — same as before this change, and that Dockerfile was already
passing.

Verified:
- docker/Dockerfile.{cpu,cuda,rdma-tools,rocm,xpu},
  guides/modelexpress-p2p/image/Dockerfile, and
  helpers/interactive-pod/build/Dockerfile all now validate cleanly
  with 'python3 scripts/lint-dockerfile-envvars.py docker/scripts <file>'
  — docker/Dockerfile.rocm's previously-flagged UCCL_PREFIX is gone.
- Two throwaway two-stage Dockerfiles confirm the fix is precise
  rather than newly permissive: a stage genuinely missing required
  vars still fails (all three flagged when none are declared
  anywhere), and ARG set in a parent stage still correctly does NOT
  satisfy a child stage's requirement (only ENV does), matching real
  Docker semantics.
- python3 scripts/lint-envvars.py $(git ls-files 'docker/scripts/**/*.sh')
  still exits 0 across all 13 scripts (this file is untouched by
  this commit).

* fix(scripts): resolve botched merge of stage-inheritance fix, defer to #2446

The 'Update branch' merge of main into this branch (aa770a7f) pulled
in PR #2446 (also merged to main while this PR was in review), which
independently fixed the same DockerfileParser stage-inheritance gap
this PR's 46874f9c addressed. The merge concatenated both
implementations instead of resolving the conflict, leaving two
competing blocks that both assign self.stages[self.current_stage] —
the second silently overwrote the first, so my ENV-only version
was already dead code, just confusingly still present.

Verified empirically with  (not just by re-reading
Docker's docs) which of the two behaviors is actually correct, since
they disagree on whether a parent stage's ARG should be inherited:

  ARG GLOBAL_ARG=hello-global      # before first FROM
  FROM alpine AS base
  ARG STAGE_ARG=hello-stage-base   # inside a stage
  FROM base AS mid
  FROM mid AS child
  RUN echo          # -> empty: needs re-declaring
  RUN echo           # -> hello-stage-base: inherited,
                                    #    2 stages down, no re-declare

A stage-scoped ARG carries forward through descendant stages same as
ENV; only a *global* pre-FROM ARG needs re-declaring per stage. So
#2446's ARG+ENV inheritance is correct and my PR's ENV-only version
(reasoning from the well-known 'ARG doesn't cross stages' advice,
which turns out to only apply to global ARGs) was subtly wrong.
Removed my superseded block and kept #2446's, with a comment
capturing this distinction for the next person who has the same
'surely ARG doesn't inherit' instinct I did.

Verified:
- scripts/tests/test_lint_dockerfile_envvars.py (#2446's own
  regression test) still passes.
- Full scripts/tests/ suite: 37 passed, 1 skipped (macOS-only gap,
  unrelated — needs GNU realpath via coreutils).
- All 7 Dockerfiles in the repo (docker/Dockerfile.{cpu,cuda,
  rdma-tools,rocm,xpu}, guides/modelexpress-p2p/image/Dockerfile,
  helpers/interactive-pod/build/Dockerfile) validate cleanly.
- lint-envvars.py still exits 0 across all 13 in-scope scripts.

  quota floors below the HPA, so it composes with any of the signals and leaves
  KEDA sole owner of the HPA it generates.

path where the real error appears.

succeeds, so the service account is vestigial for this guide. Remove it together
with the annotation, the PROJECT_ID substitution it required, and the Workload
Identity race-condition note that only applied to that annotation. This also
narrows the bucket grant from a project-wide roles/storage.admin to four
permissions on a single bucket.

checkpoint has been uploaded and the process resumed, so the wait has to cover

feat(sglang): add tiered cache GKE nightly lane (#2480)

Add the nightly E2E workflow and status consolidation job for SGLang
tiered prefix cache CPU offloading on GKE GPU, closing the remaining
automated-testing gap for SGLang alongside optimized-baseline and
pd-disaggregation.

Overlay fixes required for CI execution

The lane resolves to the native/cpu overlay. Two defects there prevented
llm-d-infra from standing it up:

- Normalize HiCache CLI arguments to "--flag=value" form. llm-d-infra
  auto-detects the served model by stripping the "--model-path=" prefix
  and then discarding anything still shaped like a flag. Bare option
  values on their own list items ("write_through", "kernel") survive
  that filter, so detection returned 3 lines instead of 1 and the value
  was passed on as --model.
- Rename base/patch-sglang.yaml to base/patch-decode.yaml so
  llm-d-infra's decode_pods glob (patch-{vllm,decode}.yaml) applies the
  functional gate override. Without it the lane would stand up the
  guide's benchmark topology of 8 replicas at TP=2.

Memory sizing

Raise decode container memory limits from 400Gi to 512Gi and requests
from 200Gi to 400Gi. --hicache-size is per TP rank, so 200 at TP=2 pins
roughly 372.5 GiB of host memory; together with the 20Gi memory-backed
/dev/shm volume charged to the same cgroup, a 400Gi limit left no room
for the Python and CUDA runtime allocations.

The fs overlay

The fs overlay is not exercised by this lane, which runs cpu only. It is
fixed here because it carries the identical model-detection defect (5
bare values instead of 3) and would fail the moment CI is pointed at it.
The change is limited to the argument form and one wrong field name in a
comment.

Behaviour for anyone following the guide by hand is unchanged: the
rendered args are equivalent and the default replica count is the same.

Workflow scheduling and isolation

Schedule the lane at 18:30 UTC daily, 3 hours after P/D SGLang on the
same cluster, with status consolidation at 20:30 UTC. Assign a dedicated
namespace, helm release (llmdbenchcicdr-gke-sglang-tiered), and runner
workspace directory (/tmp/llmdbenchcicdk-gke-sglang-tiered) so runs do
not collide with sibling GKE lanes.

Testing

Replayed llm-d-infra's model detection pipeline against all four sglang
overlays: each returns exactly one line, Qwen/Qwen3-32B, where cpu/gke
previously returned 3 and fs/gke 5. Also verified kustomize rendering,
yamllint, and the nightly matrix.

  pre-commit run --files \
    .github/workflows/nightly-e2e-tiered-prefix-cache-gke-cpu-gpu-sglang-native.yaml \
    .github/workflows/consolidate-status-tiered-prefix-cache-gke-cpu-gpu-sglang-native.yaml \
    guides/tiered-prefix-cache/modelserver/gpu/sglang/base/kustomization.yaml \

* pd-disaggregation: cache model weights on the node for the TPU overlays

Mount a node-local HuggingFace cache (hostPath /var/cache/huggingface,
HF_HOME=/root/.cache/huggingface) in the TPU base patches and in the
TPU7x dynamic-slice manifests, matching modelserver/gpu/vllm/gke/base.

Without it the model server downloaded weights into the container's
writable layer, so every container restart, including the restart after
a startup-probe failure, downloaded the model again. For the TPU7x model
(Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, 406 GB on disk) a repeated download on a
node with other data on the boot disk triggered kubelet ephemeral-storage
eviction of both the prefill and decode pods.

Document the cache location and the boot-disk requirement in the TPU
section of the guide.

Signed-off-by: yangligt2 <yangligt@google.com>

* pd-disaggregation: pin the TPU7x overlays to vllm-tpu v0.26.0

The tpu/v7/vllm and tpu/v7/vllm-dynamic-slice overlays use
TPUConnectorHMA (tpu_inference.distributed.tpu_connector_hma). In
vllm-tpu v0.27.0 through v0.29.0 the vLLM scheduler reads
connector._kv_transfer_config through
KVConnectorBase_V1.requires_kv_delivery, but the bundled TPUConnectorHMA
skips the base-class initializer, so EngineCore fails at startup:

  AttributeError: 'TPUConnectorHMA' object has no attribute '_kv_transfer_config'

v0.26.0 predates requires_kv_delivery and works. The upstream fix is
vllm-project/tpu-inference#3566 (2026-09-12); no vllm-tpu release
contains it yet.

The shared tpu-vllm/release component stays at v0.27.0 because
tiered-prefix-cache's TPU multi-host offload (#2313) needs it. A new
tpu-vllm/release-v0.26.0 component pins only the two HMA overlays; revert
this commit once a vllm-tpu release includes the fix. The TPU v6e overlay
uses the non-HMA TPUConnector, which does initialize the base class, and
is unaffected. The regression was not caught because the nightly TPU lane
only runs tpu/v6.

Validated on GKE TPU7x (2x2x1, 1 prefill + 1 decode, standalone router):
/v1/completions and /v1/chat/completions succeed through the EPP, the
prefill engine logs the KV send and the decode engine the KV pull for
every request, and decode reports 100% external prefix-cache hits.

argument. The pd-disaggregation GKE overlays already set this.

VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS for NIXL to transfer the conv state.
